value.rationale: The subsequence-universality index is the exact threshold at which a binary subsequence disappears, relevant to deletion-tolerant word reconstruction and loss of ordered patterns. An all-scale dyadic formula with a genuine parity boundary effect and a uniform logarithmic all-prefix discrepancy is a mathematically motivated structural classification, not a short finite table. Unlike ordinary or abelian factor complexity, it measures all scattered patterns. The result provides an exact universal asymptotic coefficient for a standard but nontrivially structured automatic word, with a self-contained transfer explanation; the limitations exclude unrelated generalizations.
